fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Asking for three confirmations", "body": "Teri Hunter tells Chance Garton she did not arrive at psychic work through certainty but through testing. As a teenager she went to the Psychic Eye and began asking questions silently in her head, assuming at first that she was making the answers up. So she set a condition with whatever was answering. If this is really intuition, she said, she wanted to see a thing three times before she would count it as a message. That rule of three became her working method, and it still governs how she checks a sign today rather than accepting the first impression that arrives."}, {"title": "Spirit speaks through your own file cabinet", "body": "The central technique of the episode is what Teri learned from watching John Edward on the Sci Fi channel. Do not worry what your guides are wearing or what their names are, she says. Let them use the file cabinet of your own memories. A red apple in her mind means a teacher, a green apple means health, a mason jar means something earthy. She once heard Blake Shelton singing red over and over during a Reiki session at the Anaheim Ducks, and the client's mother turned out to be named Redadilla. The symbols are personal, and you build them like a language with a dog."}, {"title": "Mercury as the intuitive planet", "body": "Teri says her guides told her during meditation that the place to start is Mercury in your natal chart, a planet nobody thinks of as intuitive because it is filed under email and small talk. Her own Mercury sits in Scorpio near Neptune, which she credits for her pattern reading. She tells listeners to use the element. Water Mercury people should sit near a fountain or a stream, air signs should try guided meditation, fire signs should run until they hit the meditative zone. Chance notes his Mercury is in Pisces in the eighth house, opposed by a Libra moon."}, {"title": "Refusing to be Nostradamus", "body": "After 9/11, Teri gave her guides a directive. Two weeks before the attacks she was a wreck, and the death of a fireman named Angel, voted off an early season of Big Brother, left her with chills she still feels. She told spirit that if there was something she had no influence over, she did not want to know. She did not want to predict the fall of things. Her guides worked around it. Before the pandemic she saw homeschooling and people working from home without seeing the cause, and they quietly coached her for two years to clean up her diet for her immune system."}, {"title": "Withholding information so the reading proves itself", "body": "Teri makes clients write their questions down and never shows her the list. When a woman told her to tell her about her marriage, Teri pointed out that she had just handed over two pieces of information. The point is not the wow. What they know that she tells them, she says, gives weight to what they do not know that she tells them. Chance calls this the party trick, the razzle dazzle some clients wait for before they engage. Teri says she takes no credit at all, and describes callers as pre qualified leads that spirit routes to her."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Teri Hunter, intuitive astrologer, joins InnerVerse to talk about the possibilities we can unleash when we become fully conscious of the power of our free will choices in life. Through meditation and self-work, Teri has opened up her mediumistic abilities, and an intuitive capacity to connect with spiritual guides, to bring forth powerful messages from our unseen protectors & teachers. Teri's life's work involves a variety of tools for greater clarity of self-knowledge, including astrology, tarot, & Reiki. She provides regular updates on the astrological climate through her Youtube channel.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Reading the Nodal Shift", "body": "Teri explains the lunar nodes as the points where the sun and moon appear to cross, easy to find without a birth time because each placement lasts about a year and a half. She reads the south node as habitual past-life patterns to release and the north node as what the soul stretches toward, linking both to the unseen far side of the moon. As the axis moves from Scorpio and Taurus, the terrain of power and control, into the Aries and Libra axis of me and we, timed to a Cancer new moon, she expects a year in which caring for yourself becomes a way of caring for others."}, {"title": "The Comfort Trap of a Libra South Node", "body": "Chance offers that the south node marks where life feels easy, which can make it a comfort trap, and wonders whether a Libra south node lets people stop worrying so much about how they come across after years of volatile division. He frames it through his own rule that anything short of a hell yes is a hell no. Teri takes it further, predicting that relationships built on one-sided service will shift in physical proximity too, drawing on two decades in Laguna Beach and her wish to be seen for who she is rather than for what she provides."}, {"title": "Malefics as the Best Friends in the Chart", "body": "Teri treats a natal chart as the weather report for the day you were born rather than a sentence you walk through for life. Saturn, in her telling, is a demanding parent who does not care which lane you choose so long as you work it well, and Pluto only held power over her through her own diminished belief in herself. Her theory of squares casts each one as a tense conversation between a habitual self and an unrooted sense of who she could become, so Pluto squaring her Mars reads as an invitation to drop resentment rather than a threat."}, {"title": "Fear as Fuel", "body": "Chance draws on his tuning sessions, where clients often carry stuck anxiety, and suggests calling that feeling excitement since it registers the same way in the body. He adds that fear arrives as a burst of energy to escape the tiger, and hesitation is where people slip. Teri sees anxiety as an inner warning that a job or relationship is off your true north, and explains why she reads the rising sign, then goes straight to the moon and leaves the sun for last: we manifest through the emotional body, so feeling not good enough will dominate, while a willingness to be afraid and try is a powerful ingredient."}, {"title": "Writing Your Own Oracle", "body": "Answering a chat question from Jenny about her decks, Teri recounts studying under Doreen Virtue despite disliking her, then losing everything she owned except the cards themselves, with no guidebooks left. That forced her to redefine each card in her own language, so an Avalon card called Letting Go became the song from Frozen, and the sword suit became the mind running its scenarios. Her guides even corrected her vocabulary in meditation, calling themselves shepherds who nudge a wandering flock rather than guides pointing a direction. Chance, for his part, still likes a reference sheet alongside his growing intuition."}]
